situation_en: Write an informal letter or email to a friend you have not seen for a long time: catch up on your news, ask about your friend’s life and suggest meeting.
Write the first three messages of a chat in an online community: two from you and one imagined reply. Introduce yourself, find something in common and ask a question.
Describe a friendship or a community group that matters to you: how it started, what you do together and why it is important.
Write a thank-you note to a person in your community, real or imagined, such as a coach or a librarian: what the person did and how it helped you.
Write a short story that starts with “I never thought I would…”. Use descriptive words for the place and the characters.
Invent a friend’s incredible story and write it in two lines. Then send messages that react with surprise and ask two follow-up questions.
Write a social post, five or six lines, about a surprising or funny moment from your week. Use two hashtags.
Write an article about why people share stories: two reasons and one example.
Write an online review of a public artwork or event, real or imagined, such as a mural, a sculpture or a street fair: what it is, what you liked, what you disliked and why people should go.
Describe a show you saw or imagine, such as dance, street theater or a concert: where it was, what happened and how the audience reacted.
Write a short post that proposes a public art project for your city: where it would be, what it would look like and one reason it would help the community.
Write a short article about how music helps people in everyday life, with two examples.
Write two short, polite email requests: ask a teacher for more time on a task and ask a friend to lend you a charger.
Write an email to a tech support team about a device that stopped working: what happened, what you tried and what you want.
Write a review of a technology product or an app: what it does, the problems you had and your final opinion.
Write an article about a technology that gives you hope for the future: what it is and why it gives you hope.
Write a letter or an email of complaint to a hotel: the problems you had, what you expected and what you want the hotel to do.
Describe an unusual hotel, real or imagined: where it is, what is special about it and who would like it.
Write advice on getting around a city you know: the best transportation, tickets and mistakes to avoid.
Write an online review of a vacation close to home or in your region: what you did and whether you recommend it.
Write a short report about how your neighborhood has changed since you were a child: what changed, what stayed the same and what you think about it.
note: O gênero do livro nesta unidade é opinion essay, que fica no gerador 1. As situações abaixo são extras.

situation_en: Write an article about what it means to be a teenager today: two challenges, for example homework, social media or choosing a career, and two opportunities.
Write a group chat conversation: give your view on a city issue, such as parks, traffic or noise. Then reply politely to a different opinion that you imagine.
Describe a festival, a fair or a sports event you attended: when it happens, what people do, the atmosphere and one moment you remember well.
Write an article that explains a custom or a tradition from your region to a foreign reader (you can leave religion out): what it is, where it comes from and how people take part.
Write an email to a friend abroad to invite the friend to a traditional event: what it is, what to wear and what to expect.
Write a post about a local food tradition: what it is, when people eat it and what makes it special.
Write a paragraph saying which superpower you would choose and why. Support it with clear examples.
Write a post about a hope you have for your community: what you wish, why and what could make it happen.
Write an email to a teacher about a project you hope to do: what it is, why and what you need.
Write a profile of a person who helped young people succeed, such as a mentor, a coach or a scientist, real or imagined: what the person did and what the person achieved.
Write a news article about a good-news story at your school or in your town: a headline, what happened, a quotation from a person involved, which you can invent, and why it matters.
Your friend writes: “What did the principal say at the assembly today?” Send messages that report what you imagine was said, using “said that…”.
Write an article with tips for spotting fake news: three signs and one example about celebrities or sports.
Write an email to a newspaper editor about a story you liked: what it was and why you liked it.
Write a cover letter or an email for a volunteer or part-time job: say what talents and experience you have and why you are a good match.
Write a résumé section called “Skills and talents”: five skills, each with one example.
Write a profile of a person your age, real or imagined, with an unusual talent: what the talent is, how the person developed it and what the person does with it.
Write a post about a talent you want to develop: why, what you will do and how you will practice.
Write an email to a classmate about a misunderstanding in a group project: what you thought, what happened and how to fix it.
Your teacher writes: “Do exercises 3 and 4 for next class.” Write messages that ask for clarification: ask two questions and check your understanding.
Write a short article about how people learn: compare two methods, such as memorizing and practicing, and say what is good and bad about each.
Write a review of an innovative class, school or learning app you know: what is new, what works and what could improve.
Write a short report about a business or a service in your area: what it offers, who uses it and one idea to improve it.
Negotiate in a text chat. Write both sides, the buyer and the seller: you want to buy a used item (a bike, a phone or a guitar), ask for a lower price, give a reason and agree on a final price.
Write an ad for a new small business idea in your town: what it offers, who it is for and why it is useful.
Write an article about a new business trend, such as sharing, repairing or renting, and what it means for people.
